title: How Many TVs Do Americans Have at Home?
paragraphs: You want to watch a movie, but your partner wants to watch a sports game. Do you take turns, try to agree on something — or simply watch in different rooms?
According to an analysis by research company YouGov, most US adults have more than one television at home, so they're probably going for that last option.
Two was the most common setup, with 25% of Americans having a pair of TVs. Twenty-two percent had one, while 19% had three.
Having more than three was much less common. Eleven percent had four TVs, 5% had five and 2% had six. A further 2% said they had seven or more.
However, 14% had no television at all!
Bigger main screens were more common in households with more TVs.
For example, among those with one television, 19% had a screen larger than 50 inches. But among those with four or more, that number was 56%.
Half of Americans said their main set was a smart TV, while 21% said they didn't know what type their main television was.
But how much time do Americans actually spend watching all those TVs?
According to the US Bureau of Labor Statistics, people aged 15 and over spent an average of 2.6 hours a day watching television in 2025.
That was more time than they spent on any other leisure activity, including socializing, reading and exercise — and about half of their total leisure time.
